title: Synthetic web shell with an impact claim resting only on file names

provenance.method: Fictional IIS and $MFT name rows written for this corpus (#1967).

seedEvents.description: IIS log on WEB-01 (shop.example.com): POST /uploads/img.aspx from 203.0.113.50 returned 200; img.aspx matched a web shell YARA rule
Directory listing of C:\inetpub\shop\checkout on WEB-01 names payment.js, payment.js.bak and cardform.aspx; the listing records file names only, with no timestamps, sizes or hashes
$MFT name hit: a file named skim.js exists under C:\inetpub\shop\static\js on WEB-01; no creation, modification or content record for it was collected

findings.confidenceReason: Two tools agree: the IIS POST succeeded and YARA matched img.aspx as a web shell.
findings.title: Web shell img.aspx used on WEB-01
findings.description: 203.0.113.50 posted to the web shell /uploads/img.aspx on WEB-01 and the server returned 200.

cannedOutput.attackerPath: 203.0.113.50 used the web shell img.aspx on WEB-01.
cannedOutput.summary: A web shell on WEB-01 was used. No file write or change on the checkout pages is in the evidence.

nextSteps.action: Collect the content, hashes and $MFT timestamps of payment.js and skim.js on WEB-01
nextSteps.rationale: Only file names are known; content and write times can confirm or refute tampering.

uncertainties.basis: The evidence shows only the names payment.js, payment.js.bak and skim.js.
uncertainties.gap: No write, modification or content record for these files was collected.

forbiddenConclusions.claim: The attacker modified the checkout pages or planted a card skimmer on WEB-01.
